source.title: Diverse Neural Network Learns True Target Functions
source.authors: Bo Xie; Ying-Yu Liang; Le Song

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports gradient-trained network training errors, but uses one-hidden-layer fully connected networks and MNIST rather than the benchmark and convolutional-network settings in V1. It also reports synthetic regression results that do not measure a version's classification-error outcome.
record.gate_note: Theoretical bounds and cited results are not empirical rows. Table 3 reports MNIST training errors; Table 2 reports synthetic regression errors and is recorded under fits_no_version. Figure 3's discrepancy values are not training-error results.
record.test_reason: The study investigates related optimization questions but does not test any stated version. Its MNIST results concern fully connected networks rather than V1's convolutional networks on CIFAR. Its teacher–student regression experiments measure final error, not V2's frequency of convergence to spurious minima or the effect of one or two extra neurons. Its theory gives conditional guarantees for diverse weights, without establishing gradient-descent convergence.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate but should emphasize the conditional and algorithm-independent nature of the results. The authors identify kernel-spectrum and unit-diversity conditions under which small gradients imply small loss and stationary points are global optima. They do not prove that gradient descent reaches such solutions. Their experiments generally favor discrepancy regularization for synthetic regression and consistently show slightly lower MNIST test error.
record.recipe_differences: The empirical classification result is a one-hidden-layer fully connected network trained on MNIST with discrepancy regularization; the paper's principal theoretical analysis concerns least-squares regression on uniformly distributed sphere inputs. It does not test the cited CIFAR classification recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: MNIST training error varies with width and whether discrepancy regularization is used.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 3 reports small training errors for fully connected MNIST networks of widths 200–800, with and without discrepancy regularization; regularization improves test error at every reported width.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: One-hidden-layer fully connected networks can attain small reported training errors on MNIST, and discrepancy regularization can improve their test performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 2 reports synthetic regression errors for students of widths 100–300 learning a width-100 teacher. Regularization lowers mean training error in three of four width settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Synthetic teacher–student regression error varies with student width and discrepancy regularization.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorems 1–3 bound training loss by squared gradient norm under dimension, width, kernel-spectrum and weight-diversity conditions. Section 9.1 and the conclusion explicitly leave algorithmic convergence guarantees unresolved.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sufficiently diverse one-hidden-layer ReLU networks have small least-squares loss at small-gradient solutions under the paper's assumptions.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 1 compares minimum kernel Gram-matrix eigenvalues under uniform and input-matched weight distributions; it does not compare training speed or depth.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Matching the weight distribution to the input distribution can improve the minimum kernel eigenvalue in the tested low-dimensional settings.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics
record.problems: The MNIST table reports errors but does not specify the optimizer, training duration, initialization, or uncertainty. The empirical evidence is limited to a one-hidden-layer fully connected MNIST setup, and the synthetic regression table has only five runs per width.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying training-error rows were omitted. Test-error columns and the plotted discrepancy/minimum-singular-value results were not included because they do not measure training classification error.

untested.parts: Convolutional-network training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including random or corrupted labels and the stated training recipes.
Spurious-minimum convergence frequencies as teacher and student grow together, and rescue by one or two extra student neurons within widths 6–20.
Depth degradation, identity shortcuts, and the stated alternatives for training deep networks.
Initialization effects on learning speed and trainable depth. Kernel eigenvalues and weight diversity do not establish these outcomes.
Loss and curvature dynamics relative to learning-rate stability thresholds.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: All tabulated values match the supplied text. Rows marked cannot_determine have no applicable claim version; this does not mean their numerical values are unreadable. Remove the record's V1 verdicts. Smaller-model errors and regularization differences in this MNIST setup cannot qualify the stated CIFAR convolutional-network claim.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, convolutional networks, corrupted or random labels, Adam, early stopping, and comparisons involving smaller models beyond the reported MNIST widths.
